answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing repeated, randomly assigned work whose results are checked against independently sampled peers; one identity cannot multiply the weight without multiplying completed work. A newcomer’s influence therefore rises slowly, like a tide, while a burst of freshly minted accounts looks like a plume against the ocean of established, cross-checked history. To overwhelm decisions, an attacker must fund real work and sustain many accounts long enough to build verified records, making a cheap identity flood costly and detectable.
